commandOrSteps: Set VITE_DATA_SOURCE=api, VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://e2e.test and VITE_WS_URL=wss://e2e.test; start local Vite development server at http://127.0.0.1:4189. Run node node_modules/playwright/cli.js test --config=playwright.u01-local.config.ts --project=chromium tests/e2e/auth-session.spec.ts. The temporary one-worker Desktop Chrome config used that base URL and was removed after the run. All 17 Auth browser tests passed. Then run node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/features/auth/pages/WebOTPPage.test.tsx src/features/auth/pages/WebAccountLockedPage.test.tsx; both TypeScript no-emit projects; focused ESLint and Prettier.
environment: Windows PowerShell; Node v24.19.0; Vite 6.4.3; Playwright 1.63.0; Chromium; local Vite development server in API mode; https://e2e.test handled only by Playwright route fixtures; backend and staging disconnected.
expected: POST /auth/login/mfa/verify declares HTTP 423 through AccountLocked. A status-only 423 response for a login MFA challenge must route to /w/auth/account-locked and must not create an authenticated session.
actual: Added a Playwright regression that submits the challenge ID and six-digit code, returns status-only HTTP 423 from the contract-declared MFA endpoint, and verifies the locked-account page is shown with no sign-out control. The full Auth browser suite passed 17/17 on the local Vite development server in API mode. WebOTPPage and WebAccountLockedPage focused unit suites passed 17/17; both TypeScript projects, ESLint and Prettier passed. The default staging preview intentionally blocks /w/auth/register behind its production safety boundary, so the Auth fixture suite was run in Dev/API mode instead. No backend or staging requests were made.
notes: This verifies frontend handling of a status-only response whose OpenAPI response has no content schema. It does not verify the server's lockout policy, backend/session-cookie behavior, staging, production or user acceptance. The separate registration verifyMfa purpose=register sessionCookie decision remains with the API/security owner.
